texts: good. this lands as a fireable rule — one adding event per keeper on the Cliff Path, carrying salt-bloom, that keeper's own lantern and its mire-essence, plus day 17, Year 1 and sundown, with 'each' recorded as the quantifier. It only pays out once individual keepers are actually asserted to be keepers on the Cliff Path; until then the rule sits dormant, which is normal for a universal.

mixed: the clause itself is clean (the mire-essence as the thing burning, 'slowly' as manner, past tense), but 'The mire-essence' cannot reach back to the mire-essences of the previous sentence — those exist only per-keeper inside that sentence's rule, so the translator has to mint a brand-new, unconnected mire-essence and the link between treating it and its burning slowly is lost. Re-state the range inside this sentence so the claim covers the same lanterns: 'The mire-essence in each lantern on the Cliff Path burned slowly.'
good. the cold wind, the repetition ('again'), the strike on the Cliff Path, and 'that night' resolved back to day 17 / Year 1 / night are all carried.

good. parses as the blanket denial it is — a strength-zero rule over every lantern on the Cliff Path, with 'no' recorded as the quantifier and 'went out' kept whole as one verb — and the rule is fireable.

good. the snap's ending and its three-night span are both carried. One caveat that needs no rewrite: 'night' is not one of the convertible duration units, so this three-night span cannot be compared against a span stated in days or hours.

bad: both halves of this sentence go wrong. 'kept salt-bloom in distribution' is a result expressed as a prepositional phrase, which has no licensed shape, so the parse files a flat 'salt-bloom is a distribution' atom that puts a substance-kind where an individual belongs; and 'for the rest of the autumn' has no licensed carrier for a span named by a period noun, so a compliant parse has to drop the time span altogether. Rewrite with a plain verb and a span word the translator handles: 'The Council continued to distribute salt-bloom throughout the rest of the autumn.'
